question: After stack v1.5.0 upgrade, what is the actual mechanism by which the scribe receives its expanded reading surface? Behavioral evidence (large cache reads, proportional cost curve, scribe self-report denying any git/fs/chronicle-read tool) supports inlined-context expansion at session start, NOT agentic tools. But the consumed handoff labels Phase 1.5b scribe-WITH-TOOLS. Sub-questions: Is the handoff label outdated/wrong, or does scribe have tools it does not surface in answers?
context: Supersedes the prior reading-surface open thread. Prior thread asked boot-summary vs raw-chronicle -- the answer is neither: it is a fixed expanded inlined context, capped by what is loaded at session start, blind to consumed handoffs and external state (git, filesystem). Confabulation resistance held 4/4 even with the expanded surface. Cost curve is well-shaped (proportional to retrieval depth, ~$0.0085 shallow to ~$0.095 deep, session totals ~$0.15-0.18). Discrepancy between handoff label (with tools) and scribe self-report (no tools) is itself worth resolving so it does not propagate as a wrong mental model to the next instance.
